observations: Photo 0 shows a car gearbox/transmission assembly on the ground, with torque converter/flexplate area visible and multiple hoses/wiring harnesses attached.
Photo 1 shows the same gearbox/transmission from another angle, with the top casing and attached lines/wiring visible.
No clear brand/model nameplate, part number, or vehicle fitment marking is readable in either photo.

identity.kind: gearbox / transmission (automatic-looking due to torque-converter area)

claims.claim: Direct tokunbo Japan highest grade Rogue and Altima gearbox
claims.evidence: Neither photo shows a readable label/part number/vehicle fitment confirming Nissan Rogue/Altima.
No shipping/origin documentation or readable markings in the photos.

claims.claim: Tested and working, no knock, low mileage, never opened.
claims.evidence: Photos only show the gearbox externally; no test video, mileage proof, or seal/opening proof is visible.

risks.risk: Wrong fitment (Rogue/Altima vs another Nissan or different pin count/variant) — price depends heavily on exact transmission code.
risks.proof: Ask for a clear photo of the transmission ID plate/label or stamped code (and/or the sticker with part number) plus the vehicle VIN/engine/transmission code it came from.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic used gearbox with unknown fitment risk (worst case for buyer).

risks.risk: Not actually tested/working (internal failure not visible externally).
risks.proof: Ask for a short video of the gearbox being tested (engaged in a vehicle or on a proper test rig) showing it drives without abnormal noise.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed working (worst case).

risks.risk: Condition issues like fluid leaks, damaged solenoids/valve body, or worn torque converter — not confirmable from these angles.
risks.proof: Ask for photos of the gearbox after cleaning plus close-ups of any suspected leak points and the underside; include a video showing no leaks after running.
risks.if_unproven: Price as needing inspection/possible repairs (worst case).

risks.risk: Automatic vs manual mismatch or different configuration (e.g., 2WD/4WD, pin count) affecting compatibility.
risks.proof: Ask for the transmission type details: pin count/connector count and 2WD/4WD, shown in a clear label photo or by matching to the donor vehicle specs.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the transmission ID plate/stamped code/part number (the one that determines exact model/variant).
Video proof of testing: start + engage (or test rig) showing no knocking and smooth engagement.
Photo of connector/pin count and any markings for 2WD/4WD and variant.
Photo showing seals/edges to support “never opened” (and any evidence of tampering).
response.reason: The photos show a gearbox but do not provide readable identification (part number/variant) and the seller’s “tested/working, no knock, low mileage, never opened” cannot be verified remotely without test and ID proof. Without the exact transmission code, a correct worst-case price cannot be confidently selected from the comparables.
